The Berlin arbitration gets Volume V of the Treaty of Washington papers. Its question is the northwest water boundary. George Bancroft presents the American memorial. He argues the Canal de Haro is the true boundary line. The memorial goes to Emperor William of Germany as arbitrator. Britain's case answers with its own history. An American reply follows, dated June 12, 1872.

Britain's second and final statement closes the pleadings. Its appendix treats the Hudson's Bay Company's old rights. The mid-volume papers revisit the San Juan dispute. They recall Captain Prevost's compromise offers as commissioner. They also judge Captain Pickett's troop landing there. Charts and correspondence complete the record. A line on a map fills a whole volume.
